rules.title: A file whose first two bytes are `#!` starts in code mode, and its first line is trivia
rules.divergesFromPhp: a `#!` first line is stripped by PHP but the file still needs `<?php` on line 2; here the shebang itself opens code mode, and a `<?nvs` after it is E0009

rules.title: There is no REPL and none is planned; `nvs run`, `nvs test` and `Core\Debug::dump` are the answer
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `php -a`; the loop an interactive shell serves is `nvs run` over a cached artifact and `nvs test`

rules.title: Reflection and source parsing are built into `Core`, and `Core\Ast` is the compiler's own parser
rules.divergesFromPhp: `Core\Ast` is built in where PHP needs `nikic/php-parser` or the PECL `ast` extension, and there is no `setAccessible(true)`

rules.title: Against Python, Novis claims the tool that gets handed over; "faster than Python" and "replaces Python" are forbidden
Every execution context binds `echo` to a sink, and the default sink is the terminal
rules.divergesFromPhp: `echo` in a scheduled script, a job worker or a test neutralizes control bytes rather than writing raw, and only an HTTP request makes it HTML

rules.title: Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty
rules.divergesFromPhp: `echo "\e[31m"` prints `␛[31m` rather than turning the text red, on a pipe and a terminal alike; colour is `Core\Cli\Text`

rules.title: `Cli\Text` is the terminal's one raw path, and both of its constructors neutralize their input
An `ESC` in a source literal is a compile error that names `Core\Cli\Text`
rules.divergesFromPhp: a hand-rolled `"\e[1m"` literal fails the build instead of styling the output

rules.title: Styling is a value type — `Cli\Style` and `Cli\Color` — and never a fifth grammar
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no escape string and no `<red>…</red>` markup; a style is `Cli\Style::of({...})` over `Cli\Color` values

rules.title: The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling
rules.divergesFromPhp: `posix_isatty`, `NO_COLOR` handling and `tput cols` are one profile read at start-up; a program writes `Cli\Text` and never asks what the terminal supports

rules.title: `Cli::displayWidth` measures the string the sink will write, in grapheme-cluster columns
rules.divergesFromPhp: `mb_strwidth` counts code points and sees an escape sequence as zero columns; `displayWidth` counts the substituted string, so a control byte costs one column

rules.title: There is no raw handle onto standard output or standard error, and no cursor, clipboard or title primitive
rules.divergesFromPhp: `STDOUT`, `STDERR`, `php://stdout` and `fwrite(STDOUT, …)` have no counterpart; byte-exact output names a file, and standard input is `Core\IO::stdin()` alone

rules.title: The tty belongs to the main task of a CLI program, so a `Core\Cli` member throws in a request and in a spawned isolate
rules.divergesFromPhp: a request handler cannot reach the terminal at all, where PHP-FPM's `STDOUT` quietly lands in the server log

rules.title: In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `\r`-and-overwrite progress bar and no cursor movement; `Cli::live` and `Cli::progress` hand the body a handle and paint nothing at all on a pipe

rules.title: A prompt is a `Core\Cli` member that reads the controlling terminal, and `secret` originates a `secret`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `readline()` reads standard input; `Cli::ask` reads the controlling terminal, so a piped program can still ask a question

rules.title: A prompt never blocks: no terminal or no answer in five minutes takes the `default` or throws `Cli\NotInteractive`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `readline()` in CI hangs until the pipeline kills it; here it throws, and no `timeout` option lengthens the wait

rules.title: Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region are restored on a throw, a fatal, a panic and a signal
rules.divergesFromPhp: a script that dies mid-prompt does not leave the shell in raw mode; restoration is the runtime's obligation rather than a `finally` the author remembers

rules.title: `#[Command]` builds the command table while compiling, and a duplicate name or an unbindable option fails the build
rules.divergesFromPhp: `getopt()` and hand-parsed `$argv` become a table built while compiling; a duplicate command, two options sharing a spelling, or an `#[Option]` on a type no text converts into is a compile error rather than a run-time surprise

rules.title: A command parameter is a positional argument unless it carries `#[Option]`, and its type converts and launders the word
rules.divergesFromPhp: an argument arrives as the parameter's declared type, `uint` unqualified and `string` `tainted`, instead of every option being a string in an array

rules.title: `Core\Command::run` dispatches to the handler the first word names, and help and completions are generated from the table
rules.divergesFromPhp: nobody writes a usage block or a completion script; `--help` and `bash`/`zsh`/`fish`/`pwsh` completions are read off the compiled table

rules.title: `nvs fmt` has one style, takes no configuration, and its output is a pure function of the file it is given
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `.php-cs-fixer.php`, no ruleset and no style flag; every knob php-cs-fixer and PHP_CodeSniffer expose is one fixed answer here

rules.title: The base style is PER: four-space indentation, K&R braces on control structures, Allman braces on declarations, and one canonical modifier order
rules.divergesFromPhp: PER's modifier order is enforced rather than recommended, and `else if` is always written `elseif`

rules.title: `nvs fmt` never decides where an expression breaks: the author's own line breaks are kept and only what surrounds them is normalized
rules.divergesFromPhp: php-cs-fixer and Prettier-style tools re-wrap to a column limit; here there is no line-length rule at all, soft or hard

rules.title: A string literal is rewritten to single quotes unless it interpolates or contains a single quote, and heredoc bodies and comments are never touched
A comma-separated list that spans more than one line gets a trailing comma, and a list on one line never does
rules.divergesFromPhp: php-cs-fixer's `trailing_comma_in_multiline` is a choice; here it is the only layout

rules.title: Consecutive `use` declarations are sorted by full path, ascending and case-sensitive, with no blank line between them
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no grouped `use A\{B, C};` form to order, because Novis's `use` names exactly one path

rules.title: Every construct PER never saw — qualifiers, `lateinit`, `fn` closures, `match`, object literals, shape types, enum cases, markup literals, a `?>` on its own line — has exactly one layout
`nvs fmt` lower-cases a mis-cased reserved spelling only where that spelling has no other legal meaning — a duration unit and the open tag, never a keyword or an identifier
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP's case-insensitive keywords are not normalized; `IF` is a legal class name and fixing an identifier's case is a rename, not a layout

rules.title: `nvs fmt` never inserts a visibility keyword; `nvs convert` inserts `public` as an E-tier rewrite
rules.divergesFromPhp: php-cs-fixer's `visibility_required` fixer writes the missing `public`; the formatter here never changes meaning, and the insertion happens only in `nvs convert`

rules.title: `nvs fmt` never reorders class members, because declaration order is observable in what a program prints and sends
rules.divergesFromPhp: php-cs-fixer's `ordered_class_elements` has no counterpart; a member's position is kept

rules.title: `nvs fmt` is a fixed point over the input bytes: byte-stable on every machine, and deliberately not source-independent
`nvs fmt` is a separate opt-in tool: no compiler command runs it, an unformatted file is never a diagnostic, and an editor composes it with quick fixes in the client
rules.divergesFromPhp: no `php -l`-style check ever holds a stylistic opinion, and formatting never lands in the same report as an error

rules.title: `nvs fmt` rewrites in place; `--check` writes nothing and exits non-zero naming every file that would change; `--diff` prints the diff instead
rules.divergesFromPhp: `php-cs-fixer fix --dry-run` is the habit; the flag is `--check` and its exit status is the whole contract

rules.title: A doc comment is exactly `///`; `////` and longer runs are ordinary comments, and `#` never is one
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `/** */` docblock; the PHPDoc shape is an ordinary comment nothing reads

rules.title: A `///` run attaches to the declaration below it across no blank line, and a doc comment attached to nothing is a diagnostic
A doc comment is Markdown plus `@see` and `@example`, each of which must resolve, and any other `@tag` is a diagnostic
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `@param`, `@return`, `@throws`, `@var` or `@deprecated`; what PHPDoc tags carried is the signature, an attribute or a declared capability

rules.title: Nothing requires a doc comment by default; `nvs check --strict-docs` reports a public member without one, and no autofix can satisfy it
rules.divergesFromPhp: an IDE cannot answer the check with a generated docblock, because there is no tag to generate

rules.title: `nvs doc <entry>` writes one Markdown page per class from the JSON and has no source of truth of its own
rules.divergesFromPhp: the renderer ships inside the binary rather than as a phpDocumentor-style tool a project installs

rules.title: `nvs meta --json` is the one machine-readable source of documentation, every renderer consumes it, and no renderer is authoritative for content
rules.divergesFromPhp: phpDocumentor re-derives documentation from source at every run; here nothing does, and the renderers share one JSON

rules.title: `nvs meta --json` prints the whole `Core` registry as one JSON document, and a field with nothing written is an absent key rather than an empty one
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `php --rf`, no reflection dump and no phpDocumentor pass over the standard library; one command from the binary is the reference's only input

rules.title: `nvs meta --json <entry>` emits that program's own declarations beside the `Core` registry, in the registry's own shape
`nvs agent` answers a coding agent from the registry and the embedded reference chapters in four commands, and the check loop is part of the surface
`nvs agent index` prints one derived line per registered member, carrying its signature and the capability it is gated on, and one per chapter heading
`nvs agent index` carries one derived line per configuration key, command, flag and diagnostic code, and `find` reaches each by the name a user types
Every diagnostic code carries a plain card that `nvs agent show` prints, and a terminal rendering names that command once
The primer is generated, and every refusal it states and every example it shows is proven against the compiler that ships with it
`nvs agent init` writes one pointer per harness, and no adapter ever states a language fact
The PHP front end is `php-rs-parser`, pinned, reached only through `nvs_convert::php`, and never linked into the server
rules.divergesFromPhp: no PHP binary is needed to convert, and the source is read at one declared dialect between 7.4 and 8.6 rather than under whichever PHP is installed

rules.title: `nvs convert` is one rule table read through two modes, and every branch carries a tier
rules.divergesFromPhp: a Rector run rewrites in one best-effort pass; here every rewrite is proven, annotated or commented out, and the default output is a worklist that does not run

rules.title: Names, constructs and semantic deltas each have one home, and the converter copies none of them
A tier-E rewrite names a differential case against the PHP oracle, or it is not E
`nvs convert` is a pure function of its input bytes, mode, dialect, table digest and flags
rules.divergesFromPhp: a Rector run iterates to a fixpoint and its output depends on the installed PHP; every pass here runs once, in a fixed order, and no PHP binary is consulted

rules.title: Every non-trivia input byte leaves the converter as code or as comment, and output is re-parsed before it is written
A converted site is annotated `TODO(convert:<id>)`, and `--check` publishes the tier counts as TOML
The converter never runs its input, never converts `vendor/` by default, never invents a binding and never claims compatibility
rules.divergesFromPhp: no autoloader, bootstrap or `composer install` runs, and a Composer dependency is reported against the package registry rather than ported

rules.title: The benchmark engine list is data, `total` is the CLI headline, and a missing engine never turns a build red
Usage telemetry and the update check are two independent opt-ins, both off by default, and neither ever implies the other
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP advertises itself through `X-Powered-By` and measures nothing; here nothing leaves the machine unless the operator switched it on

rules.title: A counter is `invocation.<subcommand>` from the compiled-in command table or `invocation.unknown`, and nothing derived from traffic is ever counted
`nvs telemetry show` prints the exact payload the next upload would send, and the schema, the endpoint contracts and the aggregated data are all published
An upload carries only the previous finished week, rides a short-lived user-initiated command at most weekly, and a process that has bound a socket never uploads
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no daemon, no timer and no background process; a server under load makes zero outbound telemetry connections

rules.title: An upload gets three seconds, is abandoned with its counters kept when that expires, says so, and never changes the carrying command's exit status
`nvs update-check` always reports the telemetry switch, the local and latest versions, and with telemetry on its upload history; `--json` is stable and the exit status is always 0
